Vaishali Jayesh Kothari vs Jayesh Pratak Kothari on 10 August,
2023
Author: B.V. Nagarathna

Bench: B.V. Nagarathna
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (C) No.2737/2022
 Vaishali Jayesh Kothari Pe
 Versus
 Jayesh Pratak Kothari Re
 O R D E R
During the pendency of this petition before this Court, the parties were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre to explore the possibility of an amicable settlement of their disputes.

Learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that the parties have arrived at a settlement before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre which is crystallized in the form of certain terms and conditions and filed on behalf of the parties by the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

They further submitted that the parties have filed a joint application under Article 142 of the 17:51:00 IST Reason:
Constitution seeking dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

sentences.text: While drawing our attention to the Settlement Agreement, learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that Clause 5(b) may be deleted, as Clause 5(c) is comprehensive enough insofar as the rights of the parties vis-a-vis the minor son during the Summer Vacation, Diwali Vacation and as and when otherwise possible.
In the circumstances, the submission of the learned counsel for the respective parties is placed on the record, Clause 5(b) the term of the Settlement Agreement stands deleted.
The parties are present before this Court through video conferencing facility.

When queried by this Court, they stated that they have indeed agreed to dissolve their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent and have agreed to the terms of the settlement arrived at before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

They further stated that they have no objection for Clause 5(b) of the Settlement Agreement to be deleted and that there shall be mutual cooperation between the parties insofar as custody and visitation rights of their minor son is concerned.

The parties further stated that they have arrived at a settlement before the Supreme Court Mediation Centre on their own free volition without there being any coercion or undue influence from any side.
Therefore, they stated that the application seeking divorce by mutual consent may be allowed.
We have taken on record the Settlement Agreement and the application seeking divorce by mutual consent filed under Article 142 of the Constitution and perused the same.

Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that a Demand Draft bearing No.366150 for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs only) in the name of VAISHALI JAYESH KOTHARI drawn on IDFC First Bank issued at Sangli is handed over to the learned counsel for the petitioner in full and final settlement of all claims of the petitioner on the respondent.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has acknowledged the receipt of the said Demand Draft.

It is also noticed that there are certain cases and proceedings pending between the parties as stated in Clause 9 of the Settlement Agreement which are as follows:
